items.title: See the Raconteurs Reunite for First Time in Seven Years at Jack White’s Nashville Concert
items.summary:
The Raconteurs played together for the first time since 2019 on Saturday night, turning up during the encore of Jack White's solo show at The Truth in Nashville. White, Brendan Benson, Jack Lawrence and Patrick Keeler ran through five songs, among them "Steady as She Goes" and three other tracks from the band's 2006 debut, Broken Boy Soldiers.

White telegraphed the reunion earlier in the day on social media, writing, "Inside info for any Raconteurs fans in the Nashville area, you might want to buy a ticket for Jack White's show at The Truth tonight, there just might be a little surprise." Rolling Stone reported that the set marked the band's first performance together since December 2019.

The timing lines up with a reissue already in motion. Third Man Records recently announced that its Vault subscription series would turn next to a 20th anniversary edition of Broken Boy Soldiers, packaged with a recording of the band's first-ever concert, played March 20, 2006, plus nine demos from the same period.

The Raconteurs have released three albums across two decades: Broken Boy Soldiers in 2006, Consolers of the Lonely in 2008, and Help Us Stranger in 2019, which arrived 11 years after its predecessor. Whether Saturday's appearance was a one-night event tied to the reissue and the opening of The Truth, or the start of something longer, has not been announced.

items.title: Barry Manilow’s Vegas Comeback Derailed by Bronchitis
items.summary:
Barry Manilow's return to the Las Vegas stage has been pushed back again, this time by a case of bronchitis. The delay is the latest in a run of health-related postponements that have kept the singer off the road for most of the past year.

Manilow postponed a stretch of dates on his planned US farewell tour in December 2025 after being diagnosed with lung cancer, Consequence reported. A longer-than-expected recovery forced him to shelve additional concerts as well as the start of his Las Vegas residency, which had originally been set to begin in May.

Manilow's next scheduled performance at the Westgate Las Vegas Resort & Casino is October 15th.

items.title: Box Office: ‘The Social Reckoning’ Flops With $5.5 Million Debut, ‘Other Mommy’ Tops Box Office With $27.5 Million
items.summary:
Other Mommy, the Universal and Blumhouse horror film starring Jessica Chastain as a double-jointed doppelganger, opened to $27.5 million in North America over the weekend, taking first place. Aaron Sorkin's The Social Reckoning, the other wide release, landed in fifth with $5.5 million against projections of $7 million to $8 million.

Other Mommy beat expectations despite brutal reception, carrying a 19% score on Rotten Tomatoes and a D+ CinemaScore grade from exit polls. Made for $18 million, it added $17.69 million overseas for a $45.19 million global total. "Horror movies are generally immune to a negative reception, but this is extreme," analyst David A. Gross of the newsletter FranchiseRe told Variety. "Business is going to drop sharply."

Sony's The Social Reckoning, which Sorkin wrote and directed, follows a Facebook engineer played by Mikey Madison who leaks internal documents to a reporter played by Jeremy Allen White. It drew a 54% on Rotten Tomatoes and a B- CinemaScore, and took in $3.5 million from 29 overseas markets for a $9 million worldwide start. Ticket buyers skewed older and male, a group that has been slow to come back to theaters.

The comparison to 2010's The Social Network was never going to be kind. David Fincher's film opened to $22 million almost exactly 16 years ago, grossed $224 million worldwide and won four Oscars, including one for Sorkin's screenplay. With Fincher and Jesse Eisenberg out, Sony called the new film a companion piece rather than a sequel and held the budget to $30 million, below the $40 million spent on the original.

The weekend's worst story remained Warner Bros.' Digger, which fell 60% in its second frame to $3.2 million from 3,321 theaters. The Tom Cruise satire has made $14 million domestically and $35.3 million worldwide against a production cost above $160 million, with theatrical losses that could exceed $200 million. Anne Hathaway, Jane Fonda, Guillermo del Toro and Mandy Patinkin have all publicly urged audiences to see it.

Holdovers filled out the rest of the chart. Amazon MGM's Verity took second with $11.4 million, down 64%, for $113 million worldwide; Sony's Resident Evil reboot placed third with $8.3 million and has reached $300 million globally; and Paramount's Heart of the Beast was fourth with $7.1 million, bringing it to $131.3 million worldwide against an $82 million budget.
